title: Emmy Noether: Modern LaTeX Working Corpus and Multilingual Translation Drafts (Reader-First Public Surface)
description:
This is the reader-facing Emmy Noether working record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. The July 2026 version replaces a 100-loose-file surface with a compact public layout: cumulative readers up front, the 43 English standalone papers grouped into one ZIP, source-control material grouped into one ZIP, recent source-repair/audit provenance grouped into one ZIP, and multilingual checkpoint readers grouped into one ZIP.

Open first: 00_Noether_German_Cumulative_Working_SourceControl_R796_20260705.pdf, 01_Noether_English_Cumulative_Working_Reader_RA10_20260612.pdf, and 02_Noether_Standalone_English_Papers_01_43_WorkingDrafts_20260706.zip. The source-control and audit ZIPs contain editable TeX, repair packets, and recent R781-R796 source-emphasis/audit material. The multilingual ZIP contains current public Spanish, Japanese, French, Chinese, and German checkpoint readers/TeX where available.

Status: this is a serious source-repair and translation working corpus, not OCR-only, but it is not a critical edition and not a globally certified final Noether corpus. Remaining mathematical/source-fidelity errors are expected, especially in dense formulas, tables, and places where the old scans are difficult. The German/source-control branch is the authority for downstream translations; language branches are useful working translations and should be checked against the source-control line.

Older granular repair packets remain preserved in previous Zenodo versions. Corrections can be proposed through the GitHub mirror: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Reader-first cleanup version. This version groups paper-level PDFs, source-control packets, repair/audit provenance, and multilingual checkpoints into a small number of human-readable files. It does not certify the corpus as a critical edition.
